b:
In histories born
from hidden graves,
can we expect anything but poppies?
Will a new spring arise?

Tongues that praised
now curse

Wolves
point at
one another
and howl

History put up statues,
as if of lords,
of those who enslaved
the peoples of Africa

Many hundreds of years later,
in righteous anger,
they became
symbols of disgust

Remember:
justice will be delayed,
but
it will win one day

Not even a poppy;
even grass sprouting there
would be rare
note: Written in 2020, when statues of slave traders, such as Edward Colston's in Bristol, were pulled down during the Black Lives Matter protests. Poppies are the flower of remembrance for the war dead.
